verdict.summary: Intuitive Machines is becoming a broader space-infrastructure prime, but the equity still carries financing and execution risk. Q2 revenue reached a record $206 million, more than four times the prior year, and backlog ended at $1.8 billion after $920 million of Q2 awards plus another $300 million early in Q3. The mix now includes spacecraft production, lunar delivery, mission operations, ground networks and a $600 million-plus commercial GEO satellite contract; national-security revenue rose from 3% to 30% of the quarter. Yet Q2 gross profit was only about $35.9 million before depreciation, operating loss was $47.1 million and operating cash use was $59.8 million. The company also sold stock: $235.2 million of net proceeds came through the $500 million ATM during Q2. The C- grade captures that tension. Status remains watch, with the existing $16.02 confirmation and $14.18 stop unchanged; backlog is not cash and a partial intraday reclaim is not activation.

business.overview:
Intuitive Machines now generates revenue from spacecraft production, lunar payload delivery, mission operations and communications infrastructure. Q2's $206 million included $166.7 million of product revenue, $36.7 million of service revenue and $2.8 million of grants, showing that hardware production currently drives the mix.

The AI and defense transmission channel runs through orbital and lunar data infrastructure: spacecraft collect information, ground stations move it, and mission systems process it for civil, commercial and national-security customers. The Goonhilly and COMSAT acquisition broadens coverage, while NSNS investment targets recurring network revenue rather than one-off lander missions.

The model breaks when awards fail to convert into profitable milestones. Launch or spacecraft failures, fixed-price overruns, delayed government funding, protests, supply constraints and acquisition integration can consume cash before backlog becomes revenue. The $500 million ATM provides funding but transfers part of that execution risk to shareholders through dilution.
business.moat: The emerging moat is vertical integration across spacecraft, lunar delivery, mission operations and ground communications, reinforced by NASA flight heritage and a record $1.8B backlog. It is not yet proven economically: low gross margin, program concentration and heavy capital needs mean the network must generate repeatable service revenue before the moat deserves full credit.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 GAAP revenue was $206.2M, up from $50.3M YoY, but GAAP operating loss widened to $47.1M and net loss attributable to Class A holders was $46.6M, or $0.29 per share. Product revenue was $166.7M; service revenue was $36.7M. Gross profit before D&A was approximately $35.9M, or 17.4%. Cash ended at $367.4M, while Q2 operating cash use was $59.8M. Management's non-GAAP outlook is $900M-$1.0B of 2026 revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA. The caveat is that $235.2M of net ATM proceeds funded Q2 and backlog conversion remains milestone-dependent. The official IR calendar and filings reviewed through August 28 do not announce the next earnings date, so it remains not confirmed.

filings.finding: The June 2026 Form 10-Q reports $367.4 million cash, $336.4 million long-term debt and $235.2 million net ATM proceeds from 8,259,379 Class A shares. Its August 6 cover shows a 228,924,068-share Class A plus paired Class C/OpCo economic base. At June 30, Note 17 reconciles 39,210,011 additional anti-dilutive or contingent securities, including awards, options, preferred conversion shares, warrants, escrow shares and convertible-note shares, to 264,590,764 gross economic shares before any capped-call offset.

The 2025 Form 10-K establishes Intuitive Machines' loss history, government-customer concentration, mission and launch exposure, internal-control risks and pre-acquisition balance-sheet baseline for judging 2026 expansion.
The August 13 Form 8-K furnished the direct Q2 earnings exhibit reporting $206.2 million revenue, $1.8 billion backlog and 2026 revenue guidance of $900 million to $1.0 billion.
The June 3 prospectus supplement establishes up to $500 million of Class A common-stock ATM capacity, authorizing market sales through named agents and direct dilution when shares are sold.

The June 3 automatic shelf registers broad securities capacity but does not itself identify shares sold, proceeds received or ATM usage; transaction evidence comes from the prospectus supplement and 10-Q.

The April 1 automatic shelf provides earlier registration capacity across common, preferred, debt and warrant securities; without a transaction-specific supplement it is not evidence of issuance or proceeds.

contrarianRisks: The $1.8B backlog is expected revenue, not cash, margin or guaranteed collection.
Q2 operating cash use was $59.8M and first-half capex was $33.9M.
The company raised $235.2M net through the ATM in Q2, materially increasing share count.
Q2 service revenue declined to $36.7M from $50.3M even as new product revenue drove total growth.
Launch, satellite, fixed-price and government-procurement failures can delay or destroy backlog value.
Redeemable noncontrolling interests and a shareholders' deficit complicate simple cash-minus-debt analysis.

macro.impact: LUNR is high-beta exposure to U.S. civil-space budgets, missile-defense spending and commercial satellite capex.
